items.informal_description: For a non-zero multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $, with variables indexed by $ \sigma $ and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to M $ where $ M $ is a sup-semilattice, the weighted total degree $ \text{weightedTotalDegree}'(w, p) $ (taking values in $ \text{WithBot} \, M $) equals the canonical embedding $ \uparrow $ of the weighted total degree $ \text{weightedTotalDegree}(w, p) $ (taking values in $ M $) into $ \text{WithBot} \, M $. items.informal_name: Infimum degree of an element in the additive monoid algebra
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  {A : Type u_3} →
    {T : Type u_4} →
      [inst : Semiring R] → [inst_1 : SemilatticeInf T] → [OrderTop T] → (A → T) → AddMonoidAlgebra R A → T
items.informal_description: For an element $ f $ in the additive monoid algebra $ R[A] $, this function computes the infimum (greatest lower bound) of the degrees of the elements in its support, where the support consists of the non-zero terms of $ f $. The infimum is taken with respect to the degree ordering $ D $ on the additive monoid $ A $, starting from the top element and iteratively combining with the degrees of each term in the support.

items.informal_name: Trailing Degree Equals Minimum of Support for Non-zero Polynomials
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] {p : Polynomial R} (h : p ≠ 0), p.natTrailingDegree = p.support.min' ⋯
items.informal_description: For any non-zero polynomial $ p $ over a semiring, the natural trailing degree of $ p $ is equal to the minimum element of its support, i.e., $\operatorname{natTrailingDegree}(p) = \min(\operatorname{support}(p))$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Element in Support Achieving Supremum Degree in Additive Monoid Algebra
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} {B : Type u_5} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder B] [inst_2 : OrderBot B]
  {p : AddMonoidAlgebra R A} (D : A → B), p ≠ 0 → ∃ a ∈ p.support, AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D p = D a
items.informal_description: For any non-zero element $ p $ in the additive monoid algebra $ R[M] $, there exists an element $ a $ in the support of $ p $ such that the supremum degree $ \sup\{D(a) \mid a \in \text{support}(p)\} $ is equal to $ D(a) $, where $ D $ is a degree function on the additive monoid $ M $.

items.informal_name: Support Exponents are Bounded by Polynomial Degree
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] {p : Polynomial R}, ∀ a ∈ p.support, ↑a ≤ p.degree
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, if a natural number $ a $ is in the support of $ p $, then $ a \leq \deg(p) $.

items.informal_name: Trailing Degree is Less Than or Equal to Support Elements in Polynomials
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] {p : Polynomial R}, ∀ a ∈ p.support, p.natTrailingDegree ≤ a
items.informal_description: For any natural number $ a $, if $ a $ is in the support of a polynomial $ p $ (i.e., the set of exponents with non-zero coefficients), then the natural trailing degree of $ p $ (the smallest exponent in the support, or 0 for the zero polynomial) satisfies $ \text{natTrailingDegree}(p) \leq a $.

items.type:
